A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STRATEGIST and contain readable main texts and appendices. Textual and visual comparison supports matching the algorithm, experiments, equations and relocated figures despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V2 reports original GOPS and Avalon experiments, including self-improvement comparisons, RL and LLM-agent benchmarks, feedback comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds human–agent Avalon evaluations, voting analyses and participant surveys in Section 3.1 and Appendix O.

M1.justification: The strategy tree, idea queue, population self-play, value-heuristic/MCTS executor and dialogue-guide procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 and the implementation and prompt appendices establish that the rewritten Section 2.3 and expanded Appendix D explain the existing procedure rather than introduce a new method.

E1.justification: GOPS and Avalon remain the evaluated games, but v3 substantially extends coverage to human–agent interaction. Section 3.1 and Appendix O introduce ten human participants playing six-player Avalon with five STRATEGIST agents, including dialogue and non-dialogue conditions.

E2.justification: Human players become a new primary performance comparator in Section 3.1 and Table 1, extending comparison beyond automated agents. The existing search, RL, feedback and LLM-agent comparator sets remain unchanged. The additional methods in Table 6 are literature comparisons, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new human study introduces random role assignment, dialogue and non-dialogue sessions, seven survey metrics, separate participant and experimenter ratings, and voting-correctness measurements. Section 3.1 reports 30 games, whereas Appendix O describes 40; their relationship is unexplained. Existing automated budgets and settings are retained, although some table metric labels are revised.

E4.justification: V3 adds role-conditioned approval and correct-vote analyses, seven-dimension human assessments and playstyle comparisons in Figures 3–5. These examine concealment, reasoning, cooperation and behavioral differences from humans. Existing model, search-budget, feedback and scaling analyses remain; v2 Figure 3 is relocated as v3 Figure 12.

E5.justification: V3 explicitly reports standard errors for the human comparison and replaces RL boxplots with bar/error-bar summaries. It also removes the median ± IQR/2 explanation from v2 Table 1, now Table 2. The RL comparison still specifies ten runs, and the meaning of its revised error bars is not stated; increased replication is not established.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports human and STRATEGIST win rates of 0.367 and 0.333, with standard errors 0.089 and 0.061; Figures 3–5 and 19–20 add behavioral and survey results. Existing central table scores remain unchanged, but RL uncertainty values change: for example, STRATEGIST's GOPS score against AlphaGo changes from 0.33 ± 1.21 to 0.33 ± 0.38. This is not a reported performance gain.

T1.justification: The strategy-policy objective, UCB rule, information-set PUCT equations and RL loss are retained. Appendix D expands explanations of existing pseudocode without adding substantive mathematical results, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: V3 adds headline claims of human-comparable performance and more sophisticated strategic randomization. Its introduction additionally claims higher win rates than human players, although Table 1 reports 0.333 for STRATEGIST versus 0.367 for humans. The original bi-level learning and automated-baseline claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 interprets less role-specific voting as strategic randomization that conceals identity, including Merlin deliberately limiting information leakage. It adds assessments of concealment and adaptability strengths and reasoning, deduction and cooperation weaknesses relative to humans. These interpretations are new; Appendix C's existing limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix O adds participant background, session durations and survey/rater procedures. Conversely, v3 removes the exact gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 identifier disclosed in v2 Section 3. Existing prompts, pseudocode, RL hyperparameters, hardware and project access information remain; much of expanded Appendix D restates information already present in Algorithm 1.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds focused discussion of discussion-game agents, a feature comparison in Table 6 and detailed positioning in new Appendix P. Newly discussed work includes Werewolf agents, SPAG and Agent-Pro, while several general-model and agent-memory references are removed. This substantially expands positioning against closely related agent frameworks.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, Section 2.3 is substantially condensed and reformulated, and related work is reorganized. Human evaluation becomes the first experimental subsection, while Appendix D gains six explanatory subsections and Appendices O–P are added. These accompany substantial narrative restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: V3 adds human-study Figures 3–5 and 19–20, the human-results table and the related-work matrix. The RL comparison changes from boxplots to bar charts with different axes and labels. Existing plots are resized or relocated, notably v2 Figure 3 moving to Appendix D as Figure 12.

improvement.justification: The human study, behavioral analyses, expanded research positioning and clearer method exposition add useful evidence and explanation. However, the unexplained 30-versus-40-game reporting and human-superiority claim conflicting with Table 1 weaken confidence in the new headline contribution. Removing the uncertainty definition and exact model identifier also reduces transparency. These gains and reporting harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
